groups.text: It is currently 29 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Anthropic has released an analysis showing that the primary use for its AI agent, Claude Cowork, is the mundane office work that employees typically avoid. The company examined one point two million anonymized sessions from over six hundred thousand organizations during May 2026. About half of all usage falls into business operations and text-based tasks, which Anthropic describes as the work around the work. This includes routine organizational burdens like compiling status reports, building onboarding checklists, and preparing presentations. These administrative processes often consume significant employee time but are rarely anyone's core responsibility. In contrast, software development makes up only a small share of Cowork's usage. Anthropic notes that developers generally prefer Claude Code, a specialized programming tool, for their coding needs rather than the general-purpose agent.

Russian attacks across Ukraine have killed at least five people and injured 35 others over the last twenty-four hours. Ukrainian officials report that most of the violence hit frontline regions in the south and east. In Kryvyi Rih, a Russian drone struck an industrial enterprise on Sunday morning, killing two people. Another drone killed a man near the town of Nikopol, while forces severely damaged a food industry facility in Dnipro. In Kherson, a drone dropped an explosive device on civilians overnight, killing one person and injuring two. Later that morning, Russian forces targeted a bus and a bus stop, wounding at least four more people. In total, 15 people were injured across Kherson and the surrounding oblast as attacks hit hospitals, homes, ambulances, and public transport. Meanwhile, in Sloviansk within the Donetsk region, Russian forces killed one civilian and injured six others.

Many people spending their summer vacations by the sea, ocean, or lakes often take a closer look at the aquatic greenery surrounding them. While these organisms are frequently mistaken for simple underwater foliage, biological reality is different. According to a biologist writing for The Conversation, marine algae are not actually plants. This distinction challenges the common way we categorize the flora found in our waterways. Understanding this biological nuance reveals that what looks like a plant from the shore belongs to an entirely different classification of life. It serves as a reminder that the natural world often defies the labels we instinctively apply during a walk on the beach.

Companies are facing a sharp tension between the need for operational efficiency and the desire to maintain their capacity for innovation. High operating costs and a shortage of specialized professionals have intensified this pressure, alongside stricter regulatory requirements and the demand for faster market responses. In response, businesses are moving toward hyperautomation to strengthen their competitiveness in a dynamic market. This model evolves beyond traditional automation by integrating artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotic process automation, and data analysis. Rather than simply automating repetitive tasks to cut costs, this approach orchestrates complete business processes from end to end. By connecting people, systems, and workflows, hyperautomation allows organizations to create more integrated operations. These systems can now make decisions with greater autonomy and agility, shifting the role of automation from a basic productivity tool to a core strategic asset for the modern enterprise.

France is grappling with a third heatwave since May, creating pressures that extend beyond the weather. In Paris, the operator of the Eiffel Tower has exceptionally closed the monument early at 4 p.m. over the weekend to manage the heat. This extreme weather coincides with a darker social trend; scientific studies shared by the NGO Care France indicate that heatwaves are accompanied by an increase in femicides, sexist assaults, and domestic violence. Adéa Guillot of Care France warns that authorities remain largely unaware of how climate change drives this domestic violence. Amidst these conditions, French political tensions persist. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen has been cleared to run in next year's presidential election. This legal victory comes despite an appeals court upholding her conviction for embezzlement. While the heat disrupts the capital and social safety, the ruling ensures Le Pen remains a central figure in France's upcoming electoral cycle.

Tensions are escalating in the Middle East as Iran's Revolutionary Guard has blocked the Strait of Hormuz and attacked a second freighter, citing violations of waterway regulations. The conflict has expanded into direct military strikes, with Iranian forces using ballistic missiles to target US airbases in Jordan and Qatar, specifically destroying the command center and jet maintenance hub at al-Udeid. In response, the US military is striking targets within Iran. This volatility follows the sudden death of US Senator Lindsey Graham at age 71 after a brief illness; Graham was a close confidant of President Trump and a vocal advocate for regime change in Iran. Meanwhile, in Germany, the DLRG reports a tragic spike in water fatalities. At least 99 people drowned in June, the highest number in 23 years since the heatwave of 2003. Officials warn that over 90 percent of these victims were men and boys under 30.

Germany's Ruhr Valley is facing a financial collapse as tax revenues drop and social spending rises. Cities and towns across the region are struggling to make ends meet, with Oberhausen particularly deep in the red. City Treasurer Apostolos Tsalastras notes that while the Centro shopping and entertainment center created jobs after the steel industry declined, these service sector roles pay less than previous industrial work. This has left the city with some of the lowest average incomes and gross domestic product in Germany. In a stark contrast to these economic struggles, US rapper Pitbull recently performed a show in London where he set a new Guinness World Record. He achieved this by organizing the largest gathering of people wearing bald caps. These two events highlight a sharp divide between the systemic financial instability facing German industrial hubs and the lighthearted spectacle of global pop culture.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 24 and 30 degrees and rain chances up to 8 percent.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has an all-day event for the twenty-twenty-six summer holidays in Berlin.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
